--- license: mit library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017

Technical Report 👁️

## Introduction **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** is a minor update to [**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.
| Benchmark | DS-V4.1-Flash-1017 | DS-V4.1-Flash | K3 | GLM-5.3 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Opus 5 | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | HLE w/o tools | 42.6 (44.0†) | 36.8 (39.1†) | 43.5 | 42.0† | 44.5 | 56.3 | | Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 42.3 | 31.2 | 12.6 | 37.9 | 39.9 | 51.8 | | DeepSWE v1.1 | 77.0 | 74.2 | 67.5 | 66.9 | 73.0 | 74.0 | | ProgramBench | 29.1 | 20.3 | 17.5 | 19.0 | 23.0 | 37.0 | | NL2Repo-Bench | 68.2 | 65.4 | 58.0 | 58.0 | 56.8 | 75.3 | | Automation-Bench v1.0.6 | 60.5 | 54.8 | 46.7 | 48.8 | 45.8 | 50.3 | | Agents’ Last Exam | 35.4 | 31.8 | 27.6 | 28.5 | 26.7 | 28.6 | | Apex Bench v1.1 | 72.1 | 64.6 | 47.8 | 56.6 | 54.3 | 65.8 | | Chartography (w/tools) | 83.0 | 78.9 | 68.1 | — | 79.9 | 84.0 | | BabyVision (w/tools) | 92.5 | 89.6 | 85.7 | — | 88.9 | 94.1 | | ZeroBench-main (w/tools) | 51.0 | 49.0 | 41.0 | — | 53.0 | 52.0 |
*† denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1.* ## Prompt Encoding This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The [`encoding`](encoding/README.md) folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (`encoding.py`) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content. For production use, we additionally release [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit. It converts Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into the Conversation format, encodes them into DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 prompts or token IDs, and parses model output back into complete or streamed responses — covering thinking, tool calls, images, and generation settings. Model inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller. ## Minimal Inference Please refer to the [`inference`](inference/README.md) folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally. **Recommended sampling parameters:** | Parameter | Value | | :--- | :--- | | `temperature` | 1.0 | | `top_p` | 1.0 | | `context_window` | 1M tokens | | `max_tokens` | ≥ 256K | ## License This repository and the model weights are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseekai2026deepseekv41flash, title={DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, } ``` ## Contact If you have any questions, please raise an issue or contact us at [service@deepseek.com](mailto:service@deepseek.com).

# FLUX 3 Image Klein for ComfyUI

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the model files repackaged for [ComfyUI](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI): the distilled and base transformers in BF16, int8 and NVFP4, the text encoder in BF16 and int8, the prompt upsampler in BF16, int8 and w4a8, and the image autoencoder. The original model repositories are [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein), [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) and [FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, the `qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` file in this repository, which the workflows run by default (see [Using with ComfyUI](#using-with-comfyui)), or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours).

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Files

Place the files in the following folders:

```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   └── flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors
    ├── 📂 text_encoders/
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors
    │   └── qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors
    └── 📂 vae/
        └── flux2-vae.safetensors
```

Files with `-base-` in the name are the base checkpoint; the others are the distilled checkpoint.

| File | Content | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors` | Klein Base, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein Base, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein Base, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, BF16 | 8.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, int8 | 4.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, BF16 | 18.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, int8 | 9.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, w4a8 | 6.7 GB |
| `vae/flux2-vae.safetensors` | image autoencoder | 0.3 GB |

The BF16 transformer and the autoencoder are the same files as `model.safetensors` and `ae.safetensors` on the original repositories. The int8 files run on 8 GB GPUs such as the RTX 3070, and on GPUs without FP8 support (RTX 30 series and older). NVFP4 needs a Blackwell GPU.

## Download

One checkpoint, its text encoder and the autoencoder, straight into the ComfyUI model folders:

```sh
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy \
  diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors \
  vae/flux2-vae.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_in

# FLUX 3 Image Klein

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

![Teaser](./teaser.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the distilled checkpoint for generation and image editing. For fine-tuning, LoRA training and research, use [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, [flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup), which the reference code loads by default, or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours). Diffusers runs neither on its own; see [Prompt upsampling](#prompt-upsampling).

This repository includes the BF16 transformer and [FP8](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/fp8r) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/tree/main/variants/nvfp4) variants, together with the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder and image autoencoder.

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Download

Download the root BF16 distilled package, including its text encoder and image autoencoder, without downloading the quantized variants:

```python
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

snapshot_download(
    repo_id="black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein",
    local_dir="weights/flux-3-image-klein",
    allow_patterns=[
        "model.safetensors", "config.json", "manifest.json",
        "ae.safetensors", "text_encoder/*",
        "README.md", "LICENSE.md", "NOTICE.md",
    ],
)
```

To download a quantized distilled transformer instead, replace the three root transformer patterns (`model.safetensors`, `config.json`, and `manifest.json`) with `variants/fp8r/*` or `variants/nvfp4/*`. Keep `ae.safetensors` and `text_encoder/*` for the other components.

These files contain the model package, not a complete inference application. Use an inference implementation that supports flow-map sampling and this checkpoint format. Quantized packages need a loader that supports their format; their file size is not a measure of total GPU memory use.

## Using with reference code

The distilled checkpoint is served on the [BFL API](https://bfl.ai) as FLUX 3 Image Klein. The reference inference code is [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein).

From the reference implementation checkout, install the package and download the two components the CLI loads besides this checkpoint. The CLI reads its weights from `weights/` (set `WEIGHTS_DIR` for another root), where the download above puts this repository.

```bash
pip install -e .

# safety classifier, always loaded
hf download Falconsai/nsfw_image_detection --local-dir weights/nsfw-classifier
# prompt upsampler (18.8 GB), on by default; --no-pup sends the prompt as typed, for captions written by another LLM
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup --local-dir weights/pup

# text-to-image
python scripts/cli.py 'A chunky knitted diorama: three white cable-knit icebergs with tiny pale blue houses, a cream banner embroidered "KNITTED ICEBERG VILLAGE", a giant magenta knitted whale tail bursting from a yarn sea' \
  --model distilled --out knitted.png

# image editing; repeat --image for multiple references
python scripts/cli.py 'the same scene at night under a knitted full moon, embroidered stars above the peaks' \
  --model distilled --image knitted.png --out knitted_night.png
```

## Using with Diffusers

FLUX 3 Image Klein uses a modular pipeline. Pass `prompt` for text-to-image generation, or pass `image` with a prompt for editing; `image` can be one image or a list of reference images. The model takes full scene captions, not short prompts: a request sent as typed gives generic output. # Fish Audio Drama 3

**Fish Audio Drama 3** is Fish Audio's new-generation text-to-speech model, built for multi-character
scenes and long-form content. It supports multi-speaker generation, voice cloning and
natural-language control.

- **35B parameters, 3B active per token**: MoE text backbone with hybrid (full + linear) attention
- **Codebook-MTP audio decoder**: 10 codebooks decoded causally over the whole sequence
- **FP8 MoE experts** with the remaining weights in bf16
- **Speaker tags** `<|speaker:0|>` … `<|speaker:15|>` — one text can carry up to 16 characters
- **Long text** is chunked automatically and can be streamed per chunk

## Launch with SGLang Omni

Drama 3 runs on [SGLang-Omni](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/) from launch day.  For installation, deployment, and streaming API examples, see the [Drama 3 Cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/fishaudio_drama3.html).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni.git && cd sglang-omni
uv pip install --prerelease=allow -v -e ".[fishaudio]"
```

```bash
sgl-omni serve --model-path fishaudio/drama-3 --port 8000
```

## Launch with vLLM-Omni

Drama 3 is supported in [vLLM-Omni](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni). For installation, deployment, and API examples, see the [Drama 3 vLLM-Omni Recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/fishaudio/drama-3).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni.git && cd vllm-omni
uv pip install -e .
```

```bash
vllm serve fishaudio/drama-3 --omni --port 8091
```

## Example Usage

The reference clip the samples below clone, unmodified:

The reference, `en0` — a 3.9 s clip, the same `common_voice_en_10119832.wav` the cloning example above uses, with the transcript `We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his.`:

<audio controls>
  <source src="https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33393249/en0.wav" type="audio/wav">
</audio>

### Point tags

A plain `/v1/tts` request: one reference (`en0`), no history, and the tags written into the text at the position where the event should land.

```json
{
  "text": "[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it's on you. [laughs] Well, maybe that's fair.",
  "references": [{"audio_path": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval-mini/resolve/main/en/prompt-wavs/common_voice_en_10119832.wav", "text": "We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his."}]
}
```

<audio controls>
  <source src="https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33393205/A1_point_tags.wav" type="audio/wav">
</audio>


### Editing as continuation

Just send the previous VQ tokens and sent it as normal language models do.

```json
{
  "text": "The quarterly report is due on Thursday, so please finish it by noon.",
  "references": [{"audio_path": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval-mini/resolve/main/en/prompt-wavs/common_voice_en_10119832.wav", "text": "We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his."}],
  "previous_takes": ["The quarterly report is due on Wednesday, so please finish it by noon."]
}
```

<audio controls>
  <source src="https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33393156/K1_edit_word_with_context.wav" type="audio/wav">
</audio>

A second edit chained onto the result of the first:

K5 chains a second edit: `by noon` becomes `by five`, with both earlier takes in the context.

```json
{
  "text": "The quarterly report is due on Thursday, so please finish it by five.",
  "references": [{"audio_path": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval-mini/resolve/main/en/prompt-wavs/common_voice_en_10119832.wav", "text": "We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his."}],
  "previous_takes": [
    "The quarterly report is due on Wednesday, so please finish it by noon.",
    "The quarterly report is due on Thursday, so please finish it by noon."
  ]
}
```

<audio controls>
  <source src="https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33393164/K5_second_edit_chained.wav" type="audio/wav">
</audio>

## Production Serving

All numbers below were measured on NVIDIA H200 GPUs with streaming requests on Seed-TTS English prompts. Each request clones a voice from one pre-encoded reference (`vq_codes` with its transcript) and uses `temperature` 1.0, `top_p` 0.9, `top_k` 30 and `max_new_tokens` 500. Throughput counts generated acoustic frames per second. TTFA is the time to first audio. RTF is the time from sending a request to its last audio chunk, divided by the duration of the returned audio.

| Concurrency | Throughput (frames/s) | TTFA p50 | TTFA p95 | RTF (mean) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 166.7 | 88.9 ms | 90.8 ms | 0.131 |
| 2 | 287.0 | 96.2 ms | 130.1 ms | 0.152 |
| 4 | 467.6 | 108.2 ms | 156.4 ms | 0.186 |
| 8 | 678.1 | 153.2 ms | 210.9 ms | 0.256 |
| 16 | 927.6 | 210.1 ms | 287.2 ms | 0.373 |
| 32 | 1,244.7 | 304.6 ms | 396.1 ms | 0.551 |
| 64 | 1,687.3 | 450.9 ms | 1,020.1 ms | 0.801 |

*Table 1. Drama 3 streaming performance on one H200. Each cell is the mean of four runs.*

A single stream gets its first audio in under 100 ms. At concurrency 16, audio is still generated about 2
models.description: Drama 3 is a 35B parameter text-to-speech model supporting multi-speaker generation, voice cloning, and natural language control across 40+ languages. It excels at generating multi-character scenes and long-form content with features like speaker tags and automatic long text chunking for streaming.

User guide   ·   中文用户指南   ·   ComfyUI

![MOSS-Image-Base and MOSS-Image-SFT](assets/teaser.webp) MOSS-Image-SFT is a supervised fine-tuned text-to-image model in the **MOSS-Image** family from OpenMOSS, derived from [MOSS-Image-Base](https://huggingface.co/OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-Base). It uses the same architecture and inference pipeline, supporting natural-language prompts, tag sequences, and JSON layouts for controlling text placement and object arrangement. ## Base vs. SFT In this example, SFT produces clearer text grouping and a more organized whiteboard layout. | MOSS-Image-Base | MOSS-Image-SFT | | --- | --- | | ![MOSS-Image-Base](assets/comparison/base.webp) | ![MOSS-Image-SFT](assets/comparison/sft.webp) | ## Quick start Use Python 3.10 or later and an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support. Install a PyTorch 2.9 or later build compatible with your CUDA environment, then install: ```bash pip install "diffusers>=0.38" "transformers>=5.3" "accelerate>=1.10" "safetensors>=0.6" "Pillow>=10" ``` ```python import torch from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained( "OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT", custom_pipeline="pipeline_moss_image", trust_remote_code=True, torch_dtype={"default": torch.bfloat16, "vae": torch.float32}, ) pipe.scheduler = type(pipe.scheduler).from_config(pipe.scheduler.config) pipe.to("cuda") prompt = '''A wide view of a refrigerator beside a kitchen counter with a fruit bowl. A small sticky note on the refrigerator door is handwritten in Chinese: "记得买牛奶和鸡蛋！ 牛奶两盒，鸡蛋一打。 顺便带一袋面包。"''' image = pipe( prompt, height=1024, width=1024, num_inference_steps=50, guidance_scale=3.0, uncond_skip_layers=[22], generator=torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(42), ).images[0] image.save("refrigerator_note.png") ``` The model and custom pipeline code are downloaded and cached automatically. You can also pass a complete local model directory to `from_pretrained`. The transformer and text encoder use bfloat16; the VAE and initial noise use float32. The bundled VAE uses the FLUX.2 small decoder. For the Gradio interface, CPU offload, and compilation options, follow the [project quick start](https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image#quick-start). For ComfyUI, search for **MOSS-Image** in **ComfyUI Manager** to install the native plugin. Integration into

--- license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: feature-extraction tags: - embedding - feature-extraction - sentence-transformers - multimodal-embedding - multimodal - vision - audio - video - image-feature-extraction - audio-feature-extraction - video-feature-extraction - sentence-similarity language: - multilingual library_name: transformers ---

Hugging Face | GitHub | Launch Blog | Documentation |
License: Apache 2.0 | Authors: Google DeepMind

**EmbeddingGemma 2** is an open multimodal embedding model built by Google DeepMind which maps text (incl. code), images, video, and audio inputs—and combinations thereof—into a single, unified 768-dimensional vector space. The model has 740M total parameters, combining a 270M parameter text model with modular vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders. Designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, EmbeddingGemma 2 delivers low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications, like search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), classification, and clustering. EmbeddingGemma 2 builds upon the architectural and capability advancements of Gemma 4, offering several core features:  * **Native multimodality:** Native multimodality: Unifies 4 modalities (text, images, video, and audio) in a single shared 768-dimensional embedding space. * **Multilinguality and code:** EmbeddingGemma 2 understands 100+ languages, and achieves a \~14% improvement on code tasks relative to its predecessor.  * **Flexible footprint:** Combines a 270M parameter text backbone (130M transformer \+ 140M embedder) with selectively loadable vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders, allowing developers to load only the modalities required for their use case. * **Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL):** Native support for truncated embeddings across 128d, 256d, 512d, and 768d, enabling up to a **6x reduction** in vector storage costs with minimal impact on quality. * **Context length:** 8K token context window, capable of processing minutes of audio or video. * **Task-steered representations:** Uses lightweight text instruction prefixes to optimize embeddings for different tasks (search, classification, clustering, semantic similarity, etc.). ### Model Overview | Parameters | Total | 740M | | :---- | :---- | :---- | | | **Backbone** | 130M | | | **Embedder** | 140M | | | **Modality Encoders** | *Vision:* 170M *Audio:* 300M | | **Architecture** | **Layers** | 24 | | | **Model Dimension** | 512 | | | **Hidden Dimension** | 2048 | | | **Sliding Window** | 1024 tokens | | | **Vocabulary Size** | 262,144 | | | **\# Heads** | 4 | | | **\# KV-Heads (Local/Global)** | 2/1 | | | **Local:Global** | 5:1 | | | **Attention** | GQA/MQA | | | **Activation** | Gated FFN with GELU | | | **Pooling** | Mean Pooling | | | **Projection Layer** | 512→768 | | **Input/Output** | **Supported Modalities** | Text, Images, Video, Audio | | | **Context Window** | 8,192 tokens | | | **Native Output Dimension** | 768 | | | **MRL Truncation Dimensions** | 128, 256, 512 | ## **Benchmark Results** EmbeddingGemma 2 was evaluated across text, code, vision, visual document, video, and audio embedding benchmarks. All results reported below use the full-precision checkpoint. ### Overall Evaluation Results (768d) | Modality | Benchmark | Metric | EmbeddingGemma 2 | EmbeddingGemma 1 | | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | | *Text* | Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB, multilingual, v2) | Mean(Task), Multiple | 61.36 | 61.15 | | | Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB, code, v1) | Mean(Task), NDCG@10 | 78.68 | 68.76 | | *Image* | Massive Image Embedding Benchmark (MIEB, lite) | Mean(TaskType), Multiple | 64.64 | \- | | | Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark (MMEB v2 \- Image) | Mean(Task), Hit@1 | 57.28 | \- | | | Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark (MMEB v2 \- VisDoc) | Mean(Task), NDCG@5 | 67.84 | \- | | *Video* | Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark (MMEB v2 \- Video) | Mean(Task), Hit@1 | 50.67 | \- | | *Audio* | Massive Sound Embedding Benchmark (MSEB, Retrieval) | Mean(Task), MRR@10 | 69.54 | \- | | | Massive Audio Embedding Benchmark (MAEB) *Hugging Face*  | Mean(Task), Multiple | 49.39 | \- | ### Evaluation Results with Vector Truncation With MRL, EmbeddingGemma 2 representations can be truncated below the native 768d to 128d, 256d, and 512d representations and re-normalized. With this, model users can reduce storage requirements, with minimal quality impact down to 256d. 128d is best suited to text-only workloads. | Output Dimension | Compression Ratio | MTEB *(multilingual, v2) Mean(Task)* | MTEB *(eng, v2) Mean(Task)* | MTEB *(code, v1) Mean(Task)* | MIEB *(lite) Mean(TaskType)* | MMEB (v2) *Overall* | MSEB *(Retrieval) Mean(Task)* | MAEB *Mean(Task)* | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | 768d (Full) | 1:1 | 61.36 | 68.46 | 78.68 | 64.64 | 59.01 | 69.54 | 49.39 | | 512d | 1:1.5 | 61.17 | 68.41 | 77.24 | 64.32 | 58.38 | 69.18 | 49.21 | | 256d | 1:3 | 60.41 | 67.78 | 76.18 | 63.13 | 56.24 | 66.76 | 48.91 | | 128d | 1:6 | 57.89 | 65.68 | 71.41 | 59.06 | 45.65 | 56.71 | 46.92 | ## **Quick Start** Install the `sentence-transformers` library: ```bash pip install -U sentence-transformers transformers ``` Generate text embeddings: ```python

models.readme_content: --- license: apache-2.0 base_model: google/gemma-4-12B base_model_relation: finetune language: - en - zh pipeline_tag: text-generation library_name: gguf tags: - humanizer - transformers - safetensors - text-rewriting - rewriting - paraphrase - style-transfer - gguf - llama.cpp - gemma4 --- # humanizer **A 12B model that rewrites AI-written drafts (emails, essays, reports, forum posts; English and Chinese) so they read like a person wrote them.** It is trained to keep every number, unit, date, name and quote and to add nothing, and it runs locally. **Quick start:** get the app for **[Mac (Apple silicon)](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/releases/download/app-v0.3.2/Humanizer-0.3.2-macos-arm64.dmg)** or **[Windows](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/releases/download/app-v0.3.2/Humanizer-0.3.2-windows-x64-setup.exe)**, open it and paste a draft; it works offline. Without the app: [llama.cpp and other runtimes](#usage-without-the-app), or [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for coding agents. ## Before and after Drafts from the held-out evaluation set. For each we generated 8 samples with the Q8_0 file (llama.cpp, the app's settings) and picked the one that reads best among those the fact judge passed; it is shown unedited, and all 8 samples are [on GitHub](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/blob/main/eval/outputs/examples-12b-Q8_0_x8.json). These are picks: across the whole set the judge flagged 44 of the 420 English rewrites, 135 problems in all, 125 of them a single word or phrase. Read the result before you send it, especially numbers, dates and names. Results over the whole set are below. More examples (a forum answer, a Zhihu answer) are in the [GitHub README](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model#before-and-after). ## Results **95% judged human by Originality.ai** at its strictest setting (210 English drafts, bf16 weights, 2026-10-02): 11 of 210 rewrites were flagged as AI, against 26 for the previous release, and no AI detector was used anywhere in training. **376 of 420 English rewrites came back with no factual problem** from a strict LLM judge, measured on the `humanizer-12b-Q8_0.gguf` file you download; where it did find one, more than 9 in 10 fixes are a single word or phrase. Method, every genre and the Chinese results: [Evaluation details](#evaluation-details). ## Quantization: smaller files, closer to the full model Most GGUF files come from one `llama-quantize` pass that rounds every weight to the target type; our 2-bit, Q3 and Q4_K_M files go further. In the 2-bit and Q3 files, we measured how much each weight tensor hurts the model when it is squeezed and gave the sensitive tensors more bits and the robust ones fewer. All three were then trained layer by layer to reproduce the full model (quantization-aware training) and distilled from the full bf16 model, used as the teacher, on English and Chinese rewriting data. For the 2-bit file, a standard build of the same size picks the same next token as bf16 70% of the time; these steps take it to 81%, 85% and then 87%. The result is still an ordinary GGUF that any recent llama.cpp runs; Q6_K and Q8_0 are standard builds, because at those sizes there is almost nothing left to recover. Numbers behind every point, KL, per-file fact checks and how each file was made: [docs/QUANTIZATION.md](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/blob/main/docs/QUANTIZATION.md). All GGUF files also have their own repo: [jialinyyzz/humanizer-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/jialinyyzz/humanizer-GGUF). **[Usage without the app](USAGE.md)** · [不用 App 怎么用](USAGE.zh.md) · [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) · [GitHub](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model) · [GGUF files](https://huggingface.co/jialinyyzz/humanizer-GGUF) · [Install guide](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · [中文说明](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/blob/main/README.zh.md) > **Setting this up with an AI agent?** Point it at [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): exact files, server command, prompt byte for byte, and a self-test. ## Quick start **App:** download the `.dmg` (Mac with Apple silicon) or the Windows installer from [Releases](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/releases/latest) (current: [app 0.3.2](https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model/releases/tag/app-v0.3.2), which can import `.docx` and PDF files and keeps any passage you mark with **Create fact** word for word). On first run it suggests one of five sizes for your memory (Q8_0, Q6_K, Q4_K_M, Q3 or 2-bit, down to 8 GB machines; app 0.3.0 and later) and downloads it once; after that it works offline. Sizes and quality notes: [Files](#files). **Command line, for long documents and agents:** `pipx install git+https://github.com/sgaofen/humanizer-local-model`, then `hz paper.md -o paper.out.md` (also `.txt` and `.docx`). It uses the app or a llama-server, keeps headings, code, tables and links, rewrites the prose piece by piece and flags an
models.description: A 12B parameter Gemma finetune for text generation, specifically designed to rewrite AI-generated content (emails, essays, reports) in English and Chinese to sound more human. It preserves key details like numbers and quotes, runs locally, and is optimized for various hardware with multiple GGUF quantizations.
